title: Repair metric-serialization desync causing intermittent dashboard gaps during high-ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported dashboards showing zero datapoints and missing traces during two high-ingest windows on 2026-02-26 and 2026-02-27. Investigation shows an intermittent serialization format mismatch between the metrics-ingest workers and the indexing reconciler under peak batching (large sequence aggregation). The mismatch caused a subset of time-series to be written with a new protobuf field order that the reconciler did not recognize, producing orphaned metric shards and broken livepanel links.

Impact: Affected hosted and dedicated tenants with bursty telemetry (approx 7% of tenants during window). Symptoms: dashboard tiles returning "no data", missing trace links from span views, alerts firing for missing SLOs. Several enterprise customers escalated to support and asked for immediate remediation and backfill.

Root cause (short): A code path introduced in runtime v1.18 for compact protobuf encoding changed the deterministic field ordering when messages were batched across multiple ingest workers. The reconciler's proto decoder relied on a now-unstable encoded ordering for fast index key derivation. Under normal load the ordering was stable, but during high concurrency the new batching micro-optimization interleaved fields and produced keys that did not reconcile with existing metric index entries.

Mitigation applied: 1) Temporarily disabled the compact-encode batching optimization at runtime via feature-flag to restore deterministic ordering (hotfix deployed 2026-02-28 03:20 UTC). 2) Enabled console fallback that shows aggregated tenant-level metrics when tile data is missing so customers have continuity. 3) Published immediate customer-facing incident update and escalated customers to SEs.

Planned permanent fix: 1) Add explicit versioned wire-format header to metrics protobuf and update reconciler to use schema-aware key generation. 2) Add a one-time reconciliation job to detect orphaned shards and rewrite keys into canonical format, plus safe backfill to restore dashboard tiles. 3) Add CI tests that fuzz and stress batch encodings across worker counts to catch non-determinism.

Acceptance criteria: dashboards for affected tenants show historical and live data after backfill; orphaned_shard_count trends to zero; no new metric-serialization exceptions in logs for 72 hours post-deploy.

Rollout plan: merge runtime patch -> canary to 5% of tenants (prefer low-traffic group) -> monitor key metrics for 24h -> gradual rollout to remaining tenants. Backfill job run after >= 12h of stable canary. Communication: customer follow-ups and postmortem scheduled in Confluence.
